sources_consulted.found: Confirmed this is Gaster Hebrew MS 255 — a Sephardi rite maḥzor with rubrics in Hebrew, Judeo-Arabic, and Ladino; described as incomplete and severely damaged

Mahzor Zihron Rahel (2007, Sephardic Traditions Foundation) covers Shalosh Regalim (Pesah, Shavuot, Sukkot) in Hebrew, English, and Ladino — Sephardi rite, same tradition; Book of Prayer of Spanish and Portuguese Jews (Oxford, 1965) also complete Hebrew+English
Birnbaum (1951), ArtScroll (1985/1986), Koren Sacks (2011-2013) all provide complete modern English maḥzorim; Sephardi editions explicitly exist
Sephardic Mahzor for Pesach, Shavuot and Sukkot with English available commercially
Pinto 1761 confirmed PARTIAL — Evening Service of Rosh Hashanah and Kippur only; 1766 expansion still High Holy Days only, not a full festival cycle maḥzor

reasoning: Gaster MS 255 is a Sephardi rite maḥzor (standard canonical festival liturgy) with trilingual rubrics. This liturgy is already in complete modern English: Mahzor Zihron Rahel (2007, Hebrew/English/Ladino, Sephardic Traditions Foundation) covers all three festivals in exactly this tradition. Pinto 1761 was partial (High Holy Days only). The underlying prayers are canonical and widely translated; the manuscript's damaged/incomplete state further weakens any 'first translation' claim.
